decisions.what: J-5 was excluded from a wave that had room for it, on a semantic-collision argument rather than a file-scope one.

decisions.what: Gate arms were built with `git archive` at the pre-dispatch commit instead of by copying the live tree.
decisions.why: The standing cycle-50 instrument copies the working tree into a throwaway directory. Building both arms from a committed tree and overlaying only the one file under test makes the arms differ by exactly the change being judged. This also retires the cycle-3 tree-stability heuristic, which fired while a builder was still writing; the agent completion notification is the only real signal, and arms pinned to a commit do not need a signal at all.

decisions.what: The sealed BASELINE could not be hash-verified after the dispatch window, and that is reported as a method defect rather than glossed. The sealed GATE SCRIPT did verify.

The remedy used instead is strictly better and should replace the practice: rebuild the pre-dispatch arm with `git archive <sealed-commit>` and re-run the restored gate against it, which regenerates the baseline from a committed tree rather than trusting a restored text file. Only the CHECK needs sealing; the baseline needs a reproducible SOURCE.

The honest third option -- taken -- is to file TS-1..TS-3 blocked with a named human actor (K-5), so the finding survives into the morning report at full strength instead of being dropped, re-scoped, or silently converted into work the spec forbids. Note the severity was 'notable', not 'fundamental': cycle.md only re-aims the clock on a fundamental verdict, and that threshold was genuinely not met -- the product's SHAPE (one quiet attributed line, pipeable, stderr-clean) held up across 32 uses; only its POOL ran out. TS-4, the one finding the non-goals permit fixing (help-text repair, no flag/dependency/corpus change), is filed todo and is the natural POLISH pick for the next cycle.

The corrected assertion lives in a separate file whose own header states it was authored AFTER the baseline and therefore carries no weight as pre-committed evidence, and it ships with a negative control proving it can go red. known_issues.desc: The Attribution section's "every number here is a checked table row or a loud failure" invariant is over ASCII DIGITS only. Two spellings of a false count still pass green: an English number WORD ("Nine of those entries are rated HIGH." — the true count is 8), and a non-ASCII digit (U+FF19 FULLWIDTH NINE), since JavaScript \d without the /u flag is ASCII-only. known_issues.why_it_matters: NOT A REGRESSION, and that is measured rather than assumed: both cells are ALSO green on the pre-change arm, so neither hole was introduced and neither was ever covered. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-002-gate-closing-out.txt, which runs exactly these two cells on both arms for this purpose. The comment in the test file was weakened from "EVERY number" to "EVERY number written in digits" so the file does not overclaim, which is the part that actually matters — an invariant stated wider than it holds is worse than a narrower true one.
known_issues.remedy: Not closed, and the argument against closing is the design's own: banning English number words in this section means banning "two".."twenty" while sparing "one", because the section's live, entirely true sentence ends "...says what would settle each one." A rule with a carve-out is the "no numbers, except..." shape this design exists to avoid, and the whole value of C7 is that it is one sentence a maintainer can hold in their head. The fullwidth-digit half is cheap (add /u and a Unicode digit class) and could be done independently if anyone judges the contrived case worth the line; it is not bundled here because closing half of a boundary and reporting the boundary closed is the failure mode this repo keeps guarding against.

known_issues.desc: REPORT.md carries a LINE-COUNT claim family that nothing re-derives, and it drifts every time any test file changes. Three sites state "1511 of 2101 test lines" / "2101 lines of tests" (REPORT.md:155, :170, :440) against a measured 1978 of 3034. Unlike the corpus and triage counts — which the shipped suite asserts structurally, so they cannot go stale without turning the suite red — the line counts are asserted by nothing and are invisible to every guard in the repo. They were already false when cycle 4 began (run #2 s cycles 2 and 3 grew readme-tags.test.js by 467 lines) and J-4 s reconciliation sweep did not reach them.
known_issues.why_it_matters: It is the same structural complaint the run keeps arriving at from different directions: a number with no reader drifts silently. The corpus counts are safe because a test reads them; these are not read by anything, so the only thing standing between them and staleness is a human noticing. Small in itself — no user sees REPORT.md — but it is the doc a MAINTAINER is told to trust, which is audience #2 in SPEC.md.
known_issues.remedy: Two options, and the cheap one is probably right. (1) DELETE the line counts. They are decoration: no decision anywhere depends on knowing the test suite is 3034 lines rather than 2101, and the "1511 of 2101" framing was making a point about guard-family bloat that the J-2a/J-2b removals have since made obsolete. (2) Give them a reader — assert them from a test, the way the corpus counts are asserted — which is more machinery than the claim is worth and would add a guard whose only job is to police a number nobody needs. Option 1 is the lean. Either way it belongs to J-4 attempt 2, which is where the three sites are named.
known_issues.note_cycle_7_run2: CLOSED, and by measurement rather than by inheriting J-4's word. The three sites this issue named are all inside (or now point into) REPORT.md's "Fresh derivation table", which J-4 attempt 2 rebuilt with an explicit vintage: the preamble states "Everything below is measured at commit dbc1939", the value column is headed "Value at dbc1939", and the reader is told to re-run each command without the ref to get today's number. CONTROLS 2/2 LIVE — readme-tags is 2175 and the total 3231 at HEAD, so the gate demonstrably could have failed and did not. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-007-verify-J-8.txt. The structural complaint this issue raised (a number with no reader drifts silently) is NOT withdrawn — it is answered here by pinning the numbers to a commit instead of by giving them a reader, which is the cheaper of the two remedies it proposed.

known_issues.what: bin/aphorism.js writes to process.stdout (lines 28, 43, 48) with no error handler, so any stdout write failure surfaces as an unhandled 'error' event: ~1006 bytes of raw Node internals on stderr. Two measured instances. (a) EPIPE when a consumer closes the pipe without reading — `--list | true`, `| true`, `--list | head -0`, `--list | /nonexistent-cmd-xyz`. Realistic trigger: the downstream command fails to exec. (b) ENOSPC on a failed write exits 1, the code README documents as "no aphorism matched", so a script mistakes a full disk for an empty filter result. NOT triggered by consumers that read at least one line: head -1, head -5, sed 1q, grep -q and wc -l are all measured clean.
known_issues.settled_by: Backlog Q-1 (todo, priority 2). Handle stdout error events: exit quietly on EPIPE per Unix filter convention, and report other write failures in the tool's own one-line "aphorism: ..." convention with an exit code distinct from 1.
known_issues.resolution: RESOLVED by Q-1 (cycle 7, stdout) + Q-3 (cycle 8, stderr), and verified by RE-RUNNING KI-31 own two measured instances rather than by assuming the fixes covered them. (a) All four EPIPE reproducers it named - `| true`, `--list | true`, `--list | head -0`, `--list | /nonexistent-cmd-xyz` - now exit 0 with zero Node internals on stderr (KI-31 recorded ~1006 bytes of raw trace). (b) The ENOSPC instance, which KI-31 measured as exit 1 and therefore colliding with the documented no-match code, now exits 3 (EXIT_WRITE_ERROR) with the one-line `aphorism: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write`. Controls KI-31 listed as already-clean (head -1, wc -l) stay exit 0. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-Q-3.txt.

known_issues.what: The dashboard render harness (runs/c*-dashboard.mjs, used by cycles 3-6) substitutes the evidence block at the FIRST match of the evidence <pre> tag. dashboard.html holds three such blocks, two of them inside HTML template comments, and the FIRST is a commented one. The harness therefore reports "ok evidence block" and "MISS count: 0" while the live TARGETS-region block stays stale. Measured at cycle 6: lines 60 and 346 are commented, line 379 is live; only line 60 was being updated. A "zero MISS" render report is NOT evidence that the page a visitor sees is current. The same duplication hid a second staleness: the phase badge read BUILD through cycle 5 although the phase was REVIEW.
known_issues.settled_by: Either strip the template-comment copies from dashboard.html so exactly one evidence block exists, or make the harness select the block not enclosed in a comment and assert an EXPECTED occurrence count per anchor (it already prints counts for the other anchors, which is how the duplication became visible at all). Cycle 6 corrected the CONTENT by replacing every block still carrying the previous cycle tag, but the harness bug itself is untouched — hard rule 5 forbids editing SWARM tooling mid-run.

known_issues.what: SWARM-side cycle commits carry messages that assert contents the commits do not and cannot have. `runs/` is gitignored in the SWARM repo (.gitignore:2), so the dashboard, the per-cycle render harness and the runfile are ALL untracked there -- yet several run #3 commit subjects name exactly those three artifacts.
known_issues.detail: MEASURED at cycle 9, not inferred. `git -C /opt/swarm show --stat 76b3a01` -> subject "run #3 cycle 6: QA full pass -- dashboard render, c6 harness, runfile", contents: tmp_aph_err.txt (0 bytes) and tmp_aph_out.txt (0 bytes), 2 files changed, 0 insertions, 0 deletions. The commit contains two empty stray temp files and nothing else. The same shape applies to c2 (c2703b1). Found because cycle 9's own SWARM commit returned "nothing to commit, working tree clean" and that was CHECKED rather than shrugged off; `git check-ignore -v` confirmed runs/dashboard.html, runs/c9-dashboard.mjs and runs/current.json are all ignored by .gitignore:2.
known_issues.why_it_matters: Low severity because NOTHING IS LOST: the durable state lives in the TARGET repo, which is committed and pushed every cycle per hard rule 1 and carries .swarm/journal.md, state.json, backlog.json and every per-cycle artifact. The runfile is additionally mirrored into each journal block, which is exactly the RESUME path for a lost runfile. The defect is one of RECORD HONESTY, not data: a reader auditing the run through SWARM commit subjects would believe a dashboard render was committed there when it was not. It also means the gitignored `runs/` tree is the ONE part of the run with no version history -- a bad render overwrites the previous one irrecoverably.
known_issues.fix: Two independent halves, both for a human, neither applied (hard rule 5 fences SWARM outside runs/ and playbook/, and .gitignore is outside both). (1) Stop naming untracked artifacts in SWARM commit subjects -- or drop the SWARM-side cycle commit entirely, since the target commit is the one that carries the state. (2) Decide deliberately whether `runs/` should stay ignored; if the per-cycle harnesses and dashboards are meant to be auditable, un-ignore runs/*.mjs and runs/dashboard.html. Also worth deleting the two stray empty tmp_aph_*.txt files that DID get committed.
